problem: The crew. Ten role files live in flightcrew/crew and eleven in .claude/agents (adversary exists only there). The spec chain is byte-frozen. The core spec keeps explorer, planner, orchestrator, implementer, verifier, critic and test-builder, adds steward, adversary, interface-builder, scribe and a stronger-tier retry, and declares each role's reach in its own file with the installed settings derived from the crew folder.

questions.text: What does a characterization test of a role file assert?
questions.why: A role file is a harness document. Its frontmatter is a contract (the fields the constitution requires, the tools it may hold, isolation and permission mode); its body is prose. Live behaviour is the test-builder's and the judge's business, not this suite's.

options.value: Frontmatter contract plus the roster separations: required fields present, tools within the role's declared reach, the sees and must-not-see table honoured by what the dispatch names.
Also body invariants, such as the orchestrator holding no Write or Edit and carrying an initialPrompt.

questions.text: Are the seven surviving role bodies kept as they are, or rewritten around workflows?
questions.why: If kept, the suite may pin body-level facts; if rewritten, only the frontmatter contract and the separations are stable enough to pin.

options.value: Rewritten: pin only the contract and the separations.
Kept near-verbatim: pin body invariants too.

questions.text: adversary.md exists only in .claude/agents, not in flightcrew/crew. Is it a kept role or a stray from the v1 build?
questions.why: The core spec names an adversary role; crew/ is the source of truth for roles.

options.value: A kept role that never made it into crew/; the suite treats crew/ as the source and the stray as a defect to note.
